pages.title: Things to take home
pages.content:
SHOP

( THINGS TO TAKE HOME )

( FIVE THINGS · PRICES IN £ )

Things to take home

Five things sit with the books: a monthly subscription, a three-month gift, a voucher, a Saturday seat, and a spine put back on. Every price is in pounds sterling.

Subscriptions

Gifts

Readings

Repairs

SUBSCRIPTIONS

Shelf Subscription — Monthly

£24 / month

One book a month chosen by a bookseller, to collect or with UK post included.

See it →

£70

See it →

GIFTS

£25

See it →

READINGS

Saturday Reading Seat

£5

See it →

REPAIRS

Spine Re-backing (Book Repair)

£18

See it →

( THE SHELVES BEHIND THE COUNTER )

The shelves behind the counter

The books themselves are not in that list of five. New fiction, poetry and essays are on the front table. Second-hand and rare are in the back room. The shelves run through Fiction, Poetry, Essays, Art & Photography, Architecture, Cookery, Travel & Maps, Children's, Second-hand and Rare. Shiori Books has kept them on Calder Lane since 2011, and there are about 9,000 books in the two rooms. If a book is in print and not on the shelf, a special order is free. It usually takes 2–4 working days, and we text you when it arrives. Gift wrapping, plain paper and cotton string, is £2 a book. Prices are in pounds sterling, the same in every language. Ask at the counter, or write to hello@shioribooks.example.

pages.title: The new shelves
pages.content:
NEW BOOKS

( THE FRONT TABLE )

( CHANGES EVERY TUESDAY )

The new shelves

The front table changes every Tuesday. Hanna Moreau buys what goes on it, and a book still in print can be ordered free, usually in 2–4 working days.

( THE FRONT TABLE )

The front table

Hanna Moreau buys the new books. She has done that since she and Callum Reid opened the shop in 2011. What she brings in goes on the front table first, face out, and the table changes every Tuesday. Fiction, poetry and essays lead. A book that has had its week on the table moves back to the shelf, and the next small stack takes the space. Nothing on that table is there by a distributor's plan. If you come on a Wednesday the Tuesday change is already done. If you come on a Monday the shop is closed, and the new stack waits until Tuesday morning, when the doors open again at 10:00.

If a book is still in print and it is not on the table or the shelf, we will order it. A special order is free. It usually takes 2–4 working days, and we text you when it arrives. Ravi Menon looks after orders, and he looks after the shelf subscription as well. Tell him the title and the author at the counter, or by email to hello@shioribooks.example. You do not pay for the ordering. You pay for the book when you collect it, at the price on the book.

pages.title: The Saturday reading
pages.content:
READINGS

( BACK ROOM · SATURDAY )

( DOORS 19:00 · READING 19:30 )

The Saturday reading

Every Saturday the back room keeps 30 seats. Doors at 19:00, reading from 19:30 to 20:30, £5, and that £5 comes off any book you buy that evening.

( FORMAT )

How a reading night runs

The Saturday reading is in the back room, the same room as the second-hand and rare books. Amara Osei has hosted it since 2015. Every Saturday the doors open for the evening at 19:00, and someone reads aloud from 19:30 to 20:30. There are 30 seats. A seat is £5, and the £5 comes off any book bought that evening. The shop itself is open on Saturday from 10:00 until 21:00, so the reading sits inside an ordinary shop day rather than after a locked door. You can buy the seat at the counter or from the Saturday Reading Seat page.

Children's story hour is the second Saturday of the month, at 11:00, and it is free. Lucía Ferrer hosts it. She has looked after the children's shelves since 2018. Story hour is in the morning, before the evening reading, and it does not use the £5 seat. Elin Sørensen, who has been here since 2021, looks after Saturdays and the poetry shelves, and she is often the person reading when the night is a poetry night.

pages.title: The back room
pages.content:
SECOND-HAND & RARE

( THE BACK ROOM )

( THURSDAYS · VALUATIONS FREE )

The back room

Callum Reid has bought the second-hand and rare books since 2011. The back room holds them, and on Saturday it also holds the reading.

( HOW CALLUM BUYS )

How the back room buys

Callum Reid has bought the second-hand and rare books since 2011, the year he and Hanna Moreau opened Shiori Books. The back room is his. A book comes in because he thought it belonged on these shelves, not because a list said it should. Some of what he buys stays for a long time. Some of it is on the table for a week and then goes home with someone who was looking for that exact thing. The room is also where the Saturday reading happens, after the shop day has turned toward evening.

Each find is described as it is. Where the book tells us a year, we print the year. Where it is a first edition, we say so. We do not add a grade we have not got from the book itself. If you want to know more about a particular copy, ask Callum at the counter and he will tell you what he can see.

Second-hand valuation is free, on Thursdays, by appointment. Bring the books in. We buy, or we tell you where a book should go if it is not one for these shelves. A valuation is not a repair. Spine re-backing is £18, and Tomasz Wilk does that work at the bench in this same room, in about 10 working days.

pages.title: A book a month, chosen for you
pages.content:
SHELF SUBSCRIPTION

( ONE BOOK A MONTH )

( CHOSEN BY THE 5TH · READY BY THE 10TH )

A book a month, chosen for you

Hanna Moreau or Ravi Menon chooses one book a month from a short note about your reading. It is ready by the 10th, to collect or to post in the UK.

( HOW IT WORKS )

How it works

You fill in a short reading note at the counter, or you send it by email. Three books you loved, and one you did not. That is the whole note. It is enough for someone here to see where your taste sits, and where it stops.

Hanna Moreau or Ravi Menon chooses your book by the 5th of each month. Hanna buys the new books for the shop. Ravi looks after orders and the shelf subscription. One of them picks. The book is one we would put on the front table, or one we know you have not got to yet.

It is wrapped and ready by the 10th. You can collect it from the shop, or we post it in the UK. The wrap is the shop's plain paper and cotton string. Nothing on the parcel is there to announce itself from across a room.

If you already own the book, swap it within 30 days. Tell us at the counter, or by email, and we will choose again from the same note. You do not need a new form. The first note still stands until you want to change it.

£24 / month

One book a month, to collect or with UK post included.

£70, the three-month gift: three books, one a month, with a card in your words.

Ask Ravi at the counter

( THE PRICES )

£24 / month and £70

The monthly shelf subscription is £24 / month. One book a month, chosen for you by a bookseller, to collect or with UK post included. The three-month gift is £70. Three books, one a month, with a card in your words. Both use the same choosing: the note, the 5th, the 10th, and the swap within 30 days. Prices are in pounds sterling, the same in every language. A gift voucher, if you would rather let someone choose for themselves, is a different thing at £25, a printed card with no expiry, to spend on anything in the shop. The subscription is for when you want us to choose.

( A GIFT )

Giving it to someone?

A three-month gift is three books and a card in your words. You write the card. We choose the books from a note about the person who will read them: three books they loved, and one they did not, if you know it. If you do not know, tell us what you have seen them read, and Hanna or Ravi will start from that.

Gift subscription →

pages.title: At the counter
pages.content:
AT THE COUNTER

( EIGHT SERVICES )

( PRICES IN POUNDS STERLING )

At the counter

Eight services, priced in pounds, and the same list on every page. Special orders and Thursday valuations are free. The other six are on the card.

Prices in pounds sterling. The same eight lines are on the home page and in the shop.

( SPECIAL ORDERS )

Special orders

A special order is any book still in print. The service is free. It usually takes 2–4 working days, and we text you when the book arrives. Ask at the counter, or email hello@shioribooks.example with the title and the author. Ravi Menon looks after orders. He also looks after the shelf subscription, so if what you really want is a book a month rather than one title, he will point you to that instead. You pay for the book when it comes in, at its own price. You do not pay for the ordering. If the book is already on the front table or in the back room, you can reserve it with Ravi and collect it in shop hours.

( GIFT WRAPPING )

Gift wrapping

Gift wrapping is plain paper and cotton string, at £2 a book. That is the whole of it. There is no patterned paper. The three-month shelf subscription, at £70, already includes a card in your words, and that card is part of the gift, not part of the £2 wrap. A gift voucher is separate again: £25, a printed card, spent on anything in the shop, with no expiry. If you are buying a book from the front table or from the back room and you want it covered, ask at the counter and we will wrap that book for £2. The Saturday letter, sent from letters@shioribooks.example, is the weekly note about the shop. It is not a wrapping service.

( REPAIRS )

Repairs

Spine re-backing is £18 a book. It takes about 10 working days, and it is done in the back room. Tomasz Wilk has kept the bindery bench since 2016. Bring the book to the counter on a day we are open. Tuesday to Friday those hours are 10:00–19:00, Saturday 10:00–21:00, Sunday 12:00–17:00, and Monday is closed. The repair we do at that price is the spine. If you are not sure the book should be mended at all, Thursday is the day for a second-hand valuation, by appointment, and that is free. We buy, or we tell you where the book should go. A valuation and a repair are two different visits. You can book either at the counter, or by phone on +44 131 555 0127.

Repairs

Spine re-backing £18, about 10 working days.

Done at the bench in the back room by Tomasz Wilk.

pages.title: The people who stay
pages.content:
BOOKSELLERS

( SEVEN PEOPLE )

( SINCE 2011 · TWO ROOMS )

The people who stay

Seven people keep Shiori Books. Hanna Moreau and Callum Reid opened it in 2011. The others arrived between 2015 and 2021, and they are still here.

( SEVEN NAMES )

Seven names

Seven people keep the shop, and the list is short on purpose.

They are the people you will see at the counter, in the back room, or at the bench. Regulars sometimes stay after closing to finish a chapter. The shop is still the two rooms it grew into: the front room for new books, the back room for everything Callum buys and for Saturday night.

A note from Amara Osei

A seat is £5, and that £5 comes off any book you buy before you leave. Some nights I introduce a guest and then sit down. Elin Sørensen looks after the poetry shelves and is in the room on Saturdays. pages.title: Since 2011, on Calder Lane
pages.content:
ABOUT

( SINCE 2011 )

( 27 CALDER LANE · EDINBURGH )

Since 2011, on Calder Lane

Hanna Moreau and Callum Reid opened Shiori Books in 2011 with one room on Calder Lane. The shop now holds about 9,000 books, in two rooms.

( 2011 )

One room

Hanna Moreau and Callum Reid opened Shiori Books in 2011 with one room, at 27 Calder Lane, Edinburgh EH9 1PQ. Hanna bought the new books. Callum bought the second-hand and the rare. The front table held what had just come in, and the shelves behind it held the rest. There was no back room yet, and no Saturday reading. The shop was the front room, the counter, and the two of them. That division of work has not been rearranged. Hanna still buys the new books, and the front table still changes every Tuesday. Callum still buys the old ones. The phone is still +44 131 555 0127, and the shop email is still hello@shioribooks.example. Letters, the weekly note, go from letters@shioribooks.example.

( 2015 — 2016 )

The back room, then the bench

In 2015 the shop took the back room, and the Saturday reading started there. Amara Osei has hosted it from the beginning. Doors at 19:00, reading from 19:30 to 20:30, 30 seats, £5, and the £5 comes off any book bought that evening. The back room did not stop being the second-hand room. The chairs come out on Saturday. On the other days the shelves are the point. In 2016 Tomasz Wilk set up the bindery bench in that same room. Spine re-backing is £18 a book and takes about 10 working days. People bring in a book whose spine has gone, and the book waits on the bench while the room carries on as a bookshop. Callum's buying and Tomasz's mending share the space without becoming the same job.

( 27 CALDER LANE )

( 2018 — 2026 )

Children, the subscription, the count

In 2018 Lucía Ferrer took the children's shelves, and the story hour began: the second Saturday of the month, at 11:00, free. In 2019 the shelf subscription began. Ravi Menon looks after it, with Hanna. One book a month, chosen by the 5th, ready by the 10th, £24 / month, or £70 for three months with a card in your words. You can swap a book you already own within 30 days. Elin Sørensen joined in 2021, for Saturdays and the poetry shelves. In 2026 the shelves hold about 9,000 books.

Getting here

The shop is a bus ride and a ten-minute walk from the centre of Edinburgh. The front room is step-free. The back room has one step, and there is a ramp. New books and the front table are in the front room, so a visit for the new shelves does not need the step. If you are coming for a Thursday valuation, arrange the time first. Valuations are free, by appointment, and Callum Reid does them. For a special order or a subscription note, ask for Ravi Menon. posts.title: How we mend a broken spine
posts.excerpt: Tomasz Wilk re-backs a broken spine in the back room for £18, and the book is ready in about ten working days.
posts.content:
A book comes to the counter with its spine gone and the boards still in a person's hands. Sometimes the cloth has split along the joint. Sometimes the spine is a loose piece of paper in the same bag as the book. The pages are usually fine. What failed is the part that holds the book as one object when you open it. We have done this work in the back room since 2016, which is when Tomasz Wilk set up the bindery bench. The repair is called spine re-backing. It costs £18 a book, and it takes about ten working days.

Re-backing means the spine is made again, so the book you already have can be read without shedding its covers. It is not a new binding of the whole book, and it is not a cleaning, and it is not a valuation. Those are different conversations. The one we price at £18 is the spine. Tomasz works at the bench in the back room, with the tools of that bench, and the book stays there until the ten working days are up. You do not have to know the names of the tools to leave a book with him. You do have to leave the book.

The practical path is short. Bring it in on a day the shop is open. Tuesday to Friday that is 10:00 to 19:00. Saturday the shop is open 10:00 to 21:00, because the reading runs in the evening. Sunday is 12:00 to 17:00. Monday is closed. Tell whoever is at the counter that you want the spine re-backed, and ask for Tomasz Wilk if you want to talk to him about that copy. The £18 is per book. Two books are two repairs. We will say at the counter if what you have brought is not a spine job. We would rather say so then than invent a second service we do not list.

The back room is not only a bench. Callum Reid has bought the second-hand and rare books since 2011, and they live on the shelves around the bench. On Saturday the same room becomes the reading room. Amara Osei hosts. The doors for the evening open at 19:00, someone reads from 19:30 to 20:30, there are thirty seats, and a seat is £5, taken off any book bought that evening. A book that is in the middle of a repair is not part of that evening. It stays on the bench. The room is simply small enough that both things are true of it: it sells the old books, and it mends a few of them, and once a week it listens to someone read.

People bring different kinds of copies. A second-hand book that has already lived a long time. A book bought new from Hanna Moreau's front table, read hard, and split at the joint. A book from home that is not one we sold at all. The price does not change with the story. Spine re-backing is £18, about ten working days, in the back room. If you are unsure the book should be mended, Thursday is the day to ask a different question. Second-hand valuation is free, by appointment. Callum looks at what you have brought. We buy, or we tell you where it should go. A valuation is not a down payment on a repair, and a repair is not a promise that we will buy the book afterwards. They are neighbours on the price list, and they stay separate.

The shop around the bench is the same shop as the front room. Hanna and Callum opened it in 2011 with one room, and the back room came in 2015 with the first Saturday reading. The bench followed in 2016. Lucía Ferrer's children's shelves and the story hour came in 2018. The shelf subscription came in 2019, £24 a month, chosen by the 5th and ready by the 10th. Elin Sørensen came in 2021 for Saturdays and the poetry shelves. In 2026 there are about 9,000 books at 27 Calder Lane. The repair work is a thin strand in that, on purpose. We mend the spine we say we mend. We do not take in every harm that can happen to a book, and we do not keep a public tally of how many spines have been put back.

If you want the work done, bring the book to 27 Calder Lane, Edinburgh EH9 1PQ, or phone +44 131 555 0127 and ask for the bench. Email hello@shioribooks.example if you would rather write first and say what the book is. When the ten working days are done, we will have it ready to collect. You pay £18, and you take your own book home with a spine that holds. That is the whole of the service, and it is enough.

posts.title: Paper, string and a card in your words
posts.excerpt: How a book leaves the counter as a gift.
posts.content:
Gift wrapping costs £2 a book. The paper is plain, the string is cotton, and the card is blank until you tell us what to put on it.

If you are buying a three-month shelf subscription as a present, the card is written in your words and goes into the first parcel. That subscription is £70 for three books, one a month.

A voucher is the other way to give a book: £25, a printed card, and it does not expire.

posts.title: A year of the shelf subscription
posts.excerpt: One book a month, chosen by a bookseller, for a year.
posts.content:
The shelf subscription began in 2019 with eleven people. Each fills in a short reading note: three books they loved and one they did not.

Hanna Moreau or Ravi Menon choose the book by the 5th of each month. It is wrapped and ready by the 10th, to collect or to post in the UK, at £24 a month.

If a subscriber already owns the book, they swap it within 30 days. It happens less often than we expected.

posts.title: Notes from the poetry swap
posts.excerpt: An open evening where everyone brings a slim book and leaves with another.
posts.content:
The poetry swap is an open Saturday evening. Everyone brings a slim book they love, reads a page from it, and leaves with someone else's.

Elin Sørensen keeps the poetry shelves and hosted this one. Thirty chairs, one lamp, and the books went round the room twice.
